axis: E / Lucas-Clarke follow-up: integrated stress response

mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Downstream of an unresolved lesion: even a correct ISR readout would change a consequence, not restore WWOX function. Deep recovery would need WWOX restored (card C01). Track B (Q230P class): whether the missing mutant protein state engages the ISR is not measured; nothing here is lesion-specific.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked ISR readout that a compound moves: ATF4 protein and eIF2 alpha phosphorylation (and ATF4-target transcripts) in WWOX-deficient human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge; then a functional endpoint (network, synaptic or myelin) after eIF2B activation.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX. In the fly, Atf4 signal rises only with Wwox reduction plus amyloid and Atf4 is never perturbed. In the one human knockout transcriptome the ISR target set is lower than chance (exploratory).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly amyloid model with partial RNAi; one human knockout transcriptome without amyloid; every compound datum is from another disease, mostly adult.

cellular_context.target_expression: ISR genes are expressed in neural tissue generally; the WWOX-dependent state is UNKNOWN.
cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: fly neurons (Atf4 signal, whole-mount) and bulk organoid RNA; no cell-type resolution in either.
cellular_context.coverage: UNKNOWN for any WWOX system at protein level.
cellular_context.limits: The only signed human readout points the opposite way from the fly (ISR targets lower), and the fly readout needs amyloid.

p4_card.identity: ISR attenuators: eIF2B activators (ISRIB and its clinical-stage successors), PERK-arm inhibitors, and repurposed compounds that reverse eIF2 alpha-P-mediated translational repression; guanabenz as the paediatric-experience member. Full per-compound table: lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md section 2.1.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a WWOX-dependent ISR elevation is shown in a human neural system. Today the transfer rests on a fly amyloid model; the one human knockout transcriptome does not show the signature. No Q230P or null-allele datum exists.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an ISR modulator to WWOX deficiency; coverage is DGIdb, ChEMBL, Open Targets, PubTator 3 gene censuses and eight PubMed searches on 2026-10-26, and DGIdb, ChEMBL and Open Targets are themselves empty for the eIF2B activators. A zero is a statement about those queries.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: not in the earlier hand-made series (A-D); first ISR card.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (partial benefit through a downstream lever); Track A (variant-independent), Track B conditional and unmeasured.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. If the ISR were elevated and harmful, attenuation could protect function; if it is adaptive, attenuation could add harm. Neither is measured for WWOX.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: eIF2B (five-subunit complex, EIF2B1-5, HGNC:3257-3261) or the PERK arm (EIF2AK3, HGNC:3255); direction: attenuate the ISR; context: amyloid-stressed fly neurons in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE.

external_not_wwox_evidence: eIF2B-activator trial in ALS: target engaged, no clinical benefit (adults)
eIF2B activator in a mouse amyloid model: memory and tau improved, amyloid not
guanabenz in children with vanishing white matter: non-randomised benefit with frequent adverse events
PERK inhibitor in a Parkinson mouse model: neuroprotection with signs of pancreatic toxicity

for: The fly reports a raised Atf4 signal with Wwox reduction plus amyloid (n 6, one antibody).
An eIF2B activator improved memory and tau in a mouse amyloid model.
A paediatric dataset for an ISR-attenuating drug exists in a different, eIF2B-driven disease.

GENETIC precedent in another disease (Xu 2026, PMID 41380592; read in full, manifest PMID41380592.json entries 1, 3, 30, 33, 34, 35; receipt FTR-20261027-41380592-01): in a fly model of the mitochondrial prolyl-tRNA synthetase lesion behind a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in people, pan-neuronal RNAi against GCN2 lowered the bang-sensitive fraction from about 87 to about 30 percent and RNAi against ATF4 from about 93 to about 46 percent (three vials of ten flies each; ATF4 spread about 30 to 62), and both shortened the developmental delay. Partial rescues, partial knockdowns measured in the single-RNAi lines only, seizure-like behaviour and developmental timing not separable, no compound and no ISRIB-class agent tested, no mitochondrial readout after suppression, sex not stated for the behavioural assay. It is a question-generating precedent for the ISR need, not a WWOX experiment and not a pharmacological result.
against: Without amyloid the fly Atf4 comparison was not significant (6 vs 6; no interaction test between backgrounds; not a demonstrated absence).
In the human knockout organoid the ATF4/ISR target transcripts are lower than chance (exploratory, no amyloid).
The ALS trial engaged the target and showed no benefit.
Atf4 is not perturbed in the paper: the Atf4-to-Ldh step is the authors' inference.
The paper reports that Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models, a reminder that attenuating a stress arm has a cost.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Amyloid load is the context of the fly effect; WWOX-DEE has no stated amyloid load. Adult neurodegeneration trials do not transfer to a developmental encephalopathy. The fly PARS2 precedent (the genetic precedent in the for-list) shows that an ISR can be harmful when a mitochondrial translation lesion drives it and says nothing about whether WWOX loss drives it: no link between WWOX and mitochondrial translation or OXPHOS protein abundance is established by any source read for this card.

p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Compounds range from research tools to clinical-stage; availability for WWOX research is not assessed.
p4_card.pharmacology: Per compound in compounds_and_sources.md: no eIF2B activity in ChEMBL for ISRIB or fosigotifator; DGIdb and Open Targets empty for the eIF2B complex; PERK inhibitors have enzyme potency in ChEMBL.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.

p4_card.next_measurement: Stage 1 (decides everything after it): eIF2 alpha phosphorylation, ATF4 protein and ATF4-target transcripts in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge. If not elevated, park with the reopening condition below. Stage 2 (only if elevated): an eIF2B activator versus vehicle on that readout and on one functional endpoint. In the fly: an Atf4 loss-of-function arm with the Ldh and lactate readouts. Readout design (added 2026-10-27 from the fly PARS2 reading): read the eIF2 kinases separately (phospho-GCN2 and phospho-PERK, not phospho-eIF2 alpha alone), read OXPHOS subunit protein abundance as a covariate because the one precedent ISR is driven by a mitochondrial translation lesion, and keep a basal-ISR-tone control (in that precedent GCN2 RNAi alone lowered phospho-eIF2 alpha below control). IT8 P5 additions (design only): (a) run every ATF4 protein and P-eIF2a read with and without activity silencing; (b) sample before, at and after the first network hyperexcitability (organoids: weeks 7, 10, 16) to order any rise against the network phenotype; (c) read OMA1 and OPA1 processing as an HRI-arm trigger readout that needs no DELE1 antibody; (d) only if Stage 1 is positive, test a potentiating arm beside the attenuating arm, with a target-engagement control for any GADD34-targeted compound, and read the isogenic corrected line beside the knock-out.
p4_card.value_added: Turns 'ATF4 raised' into a context-labelled need (amyloid-conditional, fly) and shows that the only signed human readout points the other way, so the first experiment is the readout, not a drug.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

not_known: Whether any WWOX-deficient human neural system has raised eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein, with or without a proteotoxic load.
Whether the fly Atf4 rise is upstream of Ldh (no Atf4 perturbation in the paper).

Whether the PERK arm or another eIF2 kinase (the paper's Discussion names GCN1/GCN2) is the one engaged; the two interactome entries behind that naming are a low-score unvalidated GCN1 prey (score 0.133, HEK293T) and a three-spectrum WWOX hit in a PERK proximity list (HEK293-T), neither showing binding or activation. In the one fly PARS2 precedent the engaged kinase was GCN2, with phospho-PERK unchanged, so a PERK-arm inhibitor would not be the matched tool there; which kinase, if any, is engaged in WWOX-deficient neural cells is unmeasured.

Whether an eIF2B activator, which acts downstream of eIF2 alpha phosphorylation and restores translation, would reproduce the genetic GCN2 or ATF4 suppression: the fly precedent does not separate the ATF4-dependent limb from the translation-repression limb and tested no compound.
Whether attenuating the ISR would help or harm a WWOX-deficient developing brain.

Whether an ATF4 protein or P-eIF2a rise in a WWOX-deficient neural system survives silencing of network activity (tetrodotoxin or an mGluR5 antagonist): group I mGluR activation raises both in minutes without an Atf4 mRNA change in normal mouse hippocampus (PMID 41706892), and WWOX-deficient systems are hyperexcitable (IT8 P5 loop 1).

Whether the ISR in a WWOX-deficient system is compensatory rather than harmful: in the AFG3L2 precedent (PMID 37804316) HRI or DELE1 loss worsens, and a GADD34-targeted compound improves, patient-cell and mouse endpoints, the opposite sign to the PARS2 fly; the AFG3L2 kinase evidence is siRNA in fibroblasts, GCN2 and PERK were not tested, and the compound's target is disputed (PMID 28447936). Attenuators and potentiators are therefore two arms of one open question, not one direction.
evidence_against: The organoid ISR target set is lower than chance (exploratory, uncorrected multiplicity across nine set tests).
No Atf4 perturbation in the source paper.
ALS trial: target engagement without benefit.
bridge_gaps_exposed: The bridge compares fly and organoid rows only where target, endpoint and context match; none match, so the directional summary is UNRESOLVED by construction.

translation.pediatric_suitability: UNKNOWN for WWOX; guanabenz paediatric experience exists in vanishing white matter (abstract-level).

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
Every disease-side row from the Drosophila article is NOT WWOX-DEE EVIDENCE; the organoid rows are exploratory transcript analyses of one deposit.
Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED in the bridge: the bridge has no network. The openFDA adapter was run separately and is recorded in lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; assay concentrations of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
